design: Two fresh AMD Milan n2d-standard-4 Debian 12 boots, one hardware thread per core, workload affinity and cgroup CPU 1. Use the same payload and default guest ASLR. Each same-ELF experiment retains #98 ascending and shuffled endpoints, and three new matched orders with the same multiset of query positions. Native references and costs are child wait4 user plus system CPU time.
schedule: Profile all ten ELF/input pairs once with the #97 ordinary instruction/REP client and once with Cachegrind data/branch simulation. Rotate nine native rounds over the four endpoint pairs. Compute all estimates and write predictions and a digest of the pre-label journal before any holdout-native process. Run nine rotated native rounds over the six holdout pairs. All completed outputs must match independently generated oracles.
methods: Ordinary baseline: ceil(ascending native median times holdout/ascending combined instruction+REP work), frozen Aonohako weights. Other methods pay for both same-ELF native endpoint medians. Midpoint weights them equally. Distance uses the sum of bit lengths of absolute successive query position deltas. Primary candidate uses simulated last-level data read misses (DLmr). Secondary uses simulated conditional branch mispredictions (Bcm). For each feature use (observed - ascending)/(shuffled - ascending), clamped to [0,1], or 1/2 for equal endpoint features. Interpolate CPU time linearly with that fraction and round up once.
qualification: Evaluate each boot independently. Primary comparison is the median absolute relative error of DLmr versus the cost-matched midpoint over six fresh program/input pairs. Also compare distance, Bcm and the single-anchor ordinary clock, worst error, per-program results, and verdicts for each fixed limit. A replicated gain requires lower primary error than the midpoint on both guests. Fixed deadline passes at equality, report native majority and unanimous misses; forecasts are offline diagnostic projections. Report costs and all out-of-endpoint cases; do not refit on the holdouts.
